sections.title: Peter's Imprisonment and Escape
observations: This section describes the dire situation of Peter, who is imprisoned by King Herod. Herod's actions are politically motivated, aiming to please the Jewish leaders by persecuting the church.
The church responds to Peter's imprisonment with fervent prayer, highlighting the power of communal prayer in times of crisis.
Peter's miraculous escape from prison, facilitated by an angel, emphasizes God's sovereignty and intervention in the lives of His people.

sections.title: Herod's Death
observations: Herod's pride and refusal to give glory to God lead to his downfall. This serves as a warning against arrogance and the importance of humility before God.
The narrative illustrates the consequences of opposing God and His purposes, as Herod meets a tragic end due to his blasphemy.

sections.title: The Growth of the Church
observations: The chapter concludes with a note on the continued growth of the church despite persecution, reinforcing the theme of God's unstoppable mission.
The contrast between Herod's demise and the church's flourishing serves to highlight God's ultimate authority and the futility of human opposition to His plans.

importantVerses.commentary: Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church. This verse underscores the power of prayer and the church's role in supporting one another during trials.
Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give God the glory. This verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of pride and the necessity of giving glory to God.

questions: What does Peter's escape from prison teach us about God's power and the effectiveness of prayer?
How does Herod's death serve as a warning to those in positions of power today?
In what ways can we apply the lessons of perseverance and faith from the early church to our own lives?
